1  VEHICLES ACT, PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND  AWARD PASSED BY THE COURT OF PRINICIPAL SENIOR CIVIL  -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-K:6477  MFA No. 202012 of 2017 JUDGE AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO.V.
VIJAYAPURA, AT VIJAYAPUR IN M.V.C.NO.493/2016 DATED 20.05.2017 BY MODIFYING THE IMPUGNED ORDER AND BE PLEASED TO ALLOW THE CLAIM PETITION BY GRANTING THE RELIEF AS PRAYED FOR BY THE APPELLANT, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken up for disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 20.05.2017 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-V at Vijayapura, (for short 'tribunal') in MVC.no.493/2016, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-V at Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Shri Sanganabasava B. Patil, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal is by claimant for enhancement of compensation on limited ground.

It was submitted that on contest, in claim petition filed under NC: 2023:KHC-K:6477 Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, (for short 'M.V. Act')
against owner and insurer, tribunal held that claimant had sustained injuries in accident caused by rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle by its driver and insurer was liable to pay compensation.

It assessed compensation of Rs.4,08,000/- as follows:
Amount
Sl . No. Heads of Compensation in Rupees 1. Injury, Pain and Suffering 50,000/-

2. Attendant Charges 15,000/-
3. Conveyance Charges 25,000/-
4. Food and Nourishment 20,000/-
5.

Medical Expenses 2,48,000/-
Loss of future amenities and Shankar vs Mr.P.Rameshkumar And Anr on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12445652/
2 6. 50,000/-
discomfort Total 4,08,000/-
4.
It was submitted that insurer had not preferred appeal against said award.

Insofar as enhancement, it was submitted that merely on ground that PW-2 - Dr.S.S.Bedar was not a Neuro Surgeon, tribunal rejected his assessment of permanent disability at 35-40% of whole body and did not award any compensation towards future loss of income.

But, tribunal accepted treatment records, while awarding compensation of Rs.2,48,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6477 towards medical expenses.
Therefore, refusal to award compensation towards future loss of income would be illegal and unsustainable and sought for passing of appropriate orders.
5. Shri Sudarshan M., learned counsel for respondent no.2 - insurer sought to support award and opposed enhancement.

It was submitted that when claimant was alleging loss of physical disability due to head injury, it was incumbent of claimant to have examined Neurosurgeon. PW-2 admittedly a General Surgeon was incompetent to assess disability due to loss of mental ability.
It was submitted that tribunal had awarded adequate compensation under other heads and same did not call for enhancement.

6. Heard learned counsel, perused judgment and award.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6477 7.

From above submission and since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement towards future loss of income, point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether tribunal was justified in not awarding any compensation towards future loss of income?"
8.
Claimant has stated that he was 36 years of age, working as agricultural coolie and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Though he failed to substantiate with specific evidence, same has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2015 adopted for purposes of settlement of cases before Lok-Adalath is Rs.8,000/-.
Same has to be considered.

To substantiate permanent physical disability, claimant relied upon Ex.P4-medical certificate, Ex.P9-discharge summary and Ex.P12- disability certificate and deposition of Dr.S.S.Bedar as PW- 2.
9.
From Exs.P4 and P9, it is seen that claimant sustained fracture injuries to his cervical spine and other injuries.
As per Ex.P12-disability certificate, PW-2 ssessed NC: 2023:KHC-K:6477 disability to extent of 25% towards lowering of IQ - Intelligence Quotient and 75% due to quadriparesis.

However, it is seen that claimant himself deposed before tribunal, there is no recording of demeanor Shankar vs Mr.P.Rameshkumar And Anr on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12445652/
3 indicating effect on any mental faculties.
Therefore, disability assessed by PW-2 in Ex.P12 cannot be considered.
Taking into account age, occupation and injuries sustained, it would be appropriate to assess future loss of income at 10%.

Thus, compensation towards future loss of income would be:
Rs.8,000/- X 10% X 12 X 15 = Rs.1,44,000/-.
Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.
10.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed.
In addition to compensation awarded by tribunal claimant is held entitled for additional compensation of Rs.1,44,000/- towards future loss of income.
Said compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. Insurer shall deposit same before tribunal within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
iv. On deposit, same shall be released in favour of claimant.

Sd/-
